title: feat(spec,plugin-approvals,rest): an unstaffed arm on the approvals inbox read returns an admin_rescue request to a caller who may override it
body:
Fixes #22725

Clause-②: yes (widening)

An `onEmptyApprovers: 'admin_rescue'` request opens on a slate that names no person (the literal `position:NAME`, or nothing). A privileged admin may decide it, but nothing put it in that admin's queue. `approverId` matches a slot against the addresses the caller names, and an admin's own addresses never equal an unstaffed `position:NAME`. So no "My Pending" listed it, the bell read 0, and a `lockRecord: true` record stayed locked until someone looked under **All**. This PR adds the one server-side arm that returns such a request to a caller who may override it. It is one vertical PR, as triage's answer A on the card directs.

## What changed

- **Contract** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`): `IApprovalService.listRequests`' filter gains ONE optional member, `unstaffed?: boolean`, with its docblock. `countRequests` takes the same filter type as `listRequests` (its first parameter), so it answers the member too. Nothing else on the filter moves: `approverId` matches exactly what it matched before.
- **Service** (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals`):
  - `awaitingRequestIds` is the one helper `listRequests` and `countRequests` both call. It returns `approverRequestIds(approverId)` ORed with `unstaffedOverridableRequestIds` when `unstaffed === true`, so the list and its paged `total` cannot disagree.
  - `unstaffedOverridableRequestIds` scans the pending requests inside the caller's organization wall (`SYSTEM_CTX`, the approver-index window). It keeps a row when the slate names no person AND `isOverrideActor(context, row.organization_id)` holds.
  - `isOverrideActor` is the only "admin" read, and there is no second notion. It is asked first as `visibleRequestIds` asks it, so a caller who may override nothing pays no scan. Then it is asked per row, as `attachViewers` asks it for `viewer.can_override`, so every added row reads `can_override: true`.
  - `slateNamesAPerson` (in `approver-address.ts`) is the shape test, now shared. The open path's three copies of the inline test that decides "decidable only by a privileged admin" read it too, so the slate the open path warns about and the slate the arm returns cannot drift apart. These are mechanical replacements and change no behaviour.
- **REST door** (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`): `unstaffed` joins `APPROVAL_REQUEST_LIST_PARAMS` and the single-valued multiplicity set. `readDeclaredQueryBoolean` reads it as `true` or `false` only. Anything else (`1`, `TRUE`, `yes`, an empty `?unstaffed=`) is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[0]` `{ field: 'unstaffed', code: 'invalid_boolean' }` through the door's `handleRouteError`. That is the envelope its `limit` / `offset` refusals answer, and the accepted set and code are runtime's `parseBooleanParam` (`?read=` on the notifications inbox). A repeated `?unstaffed=` gets the multiplicity `400`.
- **Docs**: the approvals page's list-filter paragraph names the parameter and its OR semantics.
- **Changeset**: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/rest`, all `minor`.

## The member's shape: the spec seat's contract call, on the four axes

A NEW explicit member, ORed with `approverId`, never ANDed. I judge this a contract-shape call, not a product split. The card's done-when and the filed console follow-up (objectui#12102: "My Pending and the bell include the requests the server's rescue arm returns") already place the rescue requests in My Pending and the bell.

- **Actual business need, measured.** The console asks My Pending as ONE server-side scope, and the bell as one polled request: `status=pending&approverId=IDS` in objectui `approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` (the `awaiting_me` scope, paged server-side through `limit` / `offset` / `total`) and `sharedUserFeeds.ts` (`useSharedPendingApprovalsCount`). Under an AND member, the console would need two requests merged on the client. A `ListView` over one data source cannot page that, and the bell would sum two counts. Under OR, the follow-up is one added parameter on each existing request. The badge objectui#12102 asks for is already on the wire: a rescue row reads `viewer.can_act: false, can_override: true`.
- **Long-term soundness / contract-first.** `approverId` is NOT re-meant for override actors. That would silently change a published member for every caller, including callers that never asked. The new member is opt-in and declared, and the REST door declares it in its closed set.
- **Keeping AI from writing it wrong.** The docblock states the OR, the "alone it selects rescues only", and the `false` equals absent rule, so `unstaffed: false` cannot be read as "exclude". The REST door refuses every spelling but `true` / `false`, so a guessed value never answers a `200` without the arm, a reply shaped exactly like "nothing to rescue". The member's name says what it selects, not which policy produced it.
- **Startup scope.** One member, one arm, zero new gates and zero new row fields. The client SDK is not widened (see Acceptance notes).

## Which population the arm returns, and why

The arm returns **pending requests whose current `pending_approvers` holds no user id and no email**: only `type:value` literals, or nothing at all. This is the test the open path makes before it warns "decidable only by a privileged admin", read off the stored slate as it stands, never off a flag stamped at open time. So the arm covers more than `admin_rescue`'s opening slot:

- **in:** an `admin_rescue` open on a literal (`position:NAME`, `team:NAME`) or on an empty slate (an expression or `manager` rung that resolved to nobody). It also covers a `fallback` that degraded to `admin_rescue`, a stored pre-rename literal that only the override can decide, and a slate whose last named approver acted and left only literals (pinned: `unanimous` over `[u9, position:sales_manager]` joins the arm once u9 approves).
- **in, deliberately:** a `position:NAME` slot whose position gained a holder AFTER the request opened. That holder also finds it under `approverId`, and the admin can still decide it, so the arm never shows a request its caller cannot act on. Dropping it would need a live directory read per literal, a second staffing notion beside the open path's.
- **out:** a slate that still names a person, even one who has since left. A position that "becomes unstaffed later" is this case: a position approver resolves to its holders' user ids at open time, so the slate keeps naming them. Proving they left needs a per-slot directory read that neither this arm nor the open path makes. Such a request stays reachable under **All** and through `reassign`.

## Pins and evidence (measured on this branch)

Service, through `listRequests` AND `countRequests` (`approval-service.test.ts`, `ApprovalService — the unstaffed arm (#22725)`, 9 cases):
- an `admin_rescue` request (literal slot, and empty slate) appears for a tenant admin and a platform admin, with every row reading `can_override: true`;
- it does not appear for a member. The flag adds nothing and refuses nothing, and the member pays no slate scan;
- CONTROL: a staffed request's queue is unchanged. Its approver reads the same rows and total with and without the flag, the arm never claims it, and the admin's flagless My Pending is unchanged;
- OR with `approverId`, across a paged window; `unstaffed: false` equals absent; a tenant admin's arm stops at their organization; per row, an org-less tenant admin reaches org-less rescues only; the slate as it stands; a finalized rescue leaves the arm.

REST door, unit (`rest-server-approvals-unknown-filter.test.ts` §4): `true` / `false` reach both `listRequests` and `countRequests` beside `approverId`. Absent hands no arm. `1` / `TRUE` / `yes` / empty are refused `400 invalid_boolean`, and neither service method runs. Repeated is refused by the multiplicity gate. The closed-set preservation loop sends `unstaffed` one of its own values.

Through the REST door on a real boot (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-unstaffed-arm.dogfood.test.ts`, a new two-object fixture): the card's three pins on the paged list and its `total` (the bell's number), plus the door's `400`.

Ablations, each run from a committed state with the restore proven by blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`:
- arm disabled (`if (filter?.unstaffed !== true || true) return byApprover;`): 6 of the 8 service cases red. The 2 that stay green (`false` equals absent, the tenant wall) do not depend on the arm being on.
- per-row override test deleted: the org-less tenant-admin case red, the other 8 green.
- REST reader replaced by the bare `q.unstaffed === 'true'`: 5 door cases red (the four refusals, and "absent hands no arm").
- dogfood, through `dist/`: the arm mutation rebuilt into `plugin-approvals`. `ablation-dist-preflight` confirmed the marker in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.mjs`, and the pin went red on the admin's `approverId`-plus-`unstaffed` read. After the restore, the rebuilt `dist/` had the marker absent and the tree clean.

Suites (full, not filtered), measured at the PR head `bb112188a9` (after merging `origin/main` at `996aa86e0a`):
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: 71 files, 1032 tests passed;
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: 272 files, 5247 passed, 326 skipped;
- dogfood: `approval-unstaffed-arm`, plus the two neighbouring approvals pins (`approval-override-composite-pin`, `my-pending-position-address`): 3 of 3 passed;
- `typecheck` exit 0 for `plugin-approvals` and `rest` (both run `check:test-typecheck`, which covers their test files), for `spec`, and for `dogfood`, whose `tsc` program lists both new files;
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: all 14 generated artifacts up to date. `api-surface` records the interface by name, so the member moves no snapshot.

Gates at `bb112188a9`:
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` reports 114 derived families, 114 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. Every one carries a recorded exit code, and all are 0.
- The six artifact-roster families whose roster sits beside my paths are also 0: `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:route-ledger-census`.
- The CI-only jobs and type-check lanes that derivation names are left to CI.
- Lint, narrowed and proven. eslint's own population is `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` (`eslint.config.mjs`), so the two Markdown files are outside it. All 8 changed TypeScript files were linted with `--no-inline-config --format json`: 8 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- **Client SDK not widened.** `@objectstack/client`'s `approvals.listRequests` hand-writes its filter type, and it was already a subset of the contract's (no `q`, `limit` or `offset`). The console reads the door through its own `approvalsApi`, so there is no measured consumer of the SDK method for this member. It is noted here, not filed. Carrier: none.
- **The boolean reader is a second spelling of runtime's rule.** `@objectstack/rest` cannot import `@objectstack/runtime`'s `parseBooleanParam` (runtime depends on rest). The reader's docblock names the rule it mirrors, the accepted set, and the code. Carrier: none.
- **`listRequests`' `limit` docblock in the contract**: corrected in this PR (patch round 1, `640aed576d`). It said an `approverId` / status-array filter "post-filters in memory", with the window applied after filtering, which was false at the head. It now says what the head serves: the window is engine-level for every filter (a status array pushes down as `$in`), and the two "who acts next" arms (`approverId`, `unstaffed`) first resolve to a bounded id set (the approver index and the pending scan, each within `APPROVER_INDEX_CAP`), with the window applied to that set engine-side.
- **File surface beyond the claim's list:** the docs paragraph (`content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`) and the dogfood pin plus its fixture, which carry the claim's "each pin runs through the service and through the REST door".
